audit.whatIsWrong: early says of Transfusion "it heals him and pokes, but it costs health, so auto-poke him back during the health-cost window before the heal resolves", and whys[0] says "it costs his own health to cast".
audit.why: Transfusion has no cost at all — it is pure poke and heal. The health cost in Vladimir's kit belongs to Tides of Blood (E), which "pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood". So the entry sends the player to punish a window that does not exist on Q, and the level 1-3 plan is built on it.
audit.corrected: Transfusion is free to cast. Tides of Blood is the ability that costs him health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (Q Transfusion cost 0; E Tides of Blood description)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] "Sanguine Pool's 26-second cooldown" and whys[3] "Sanguine Pool's 26-second timer".
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s — 26 is not its cooldown at any rank. The entry builds its whole trade rhythm on this number, so being two seconds early at rank 1 means walking into a pool that is still up. Rank 1 is 28s and it drops to 16s maxed, which also means the punish window shrinks steadily rather than staying fixed.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, falling to 16s at max rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Crimson Rush" in wants.foe[2] ("out-heal your DoT with Crimson Rush Q stacks") and whys[5] ("cuts through Crimson Rush healing").
audit.why: There is no ability called Crimson Rush. His passive is Crimson Pact, which converts bonus health to AP and back and does no healing at all; the healing is Transfusion (Q), on 9s at rank 1 down to 4.6s maxed. Naming the passive as the heal source also hides the real reason anti-heal timing matters, which is Transfusion's very short cooldown.
audit.corrected: Transfusion is the heal, 4.6s at max rank. Crimson Pact is the AP/health conversion passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] "Land Tides of Blood E during your short trades to stack Hemoplague stacks".
audit.why: Tides of Blood does not feed Hemoplague — it is a self-charging AoE that costs Vladimir health, and Hemoplague is an independent zone ult that amplifies damage. More usefully, Riot's own Tides of Blood text ends "but can be blocked by enemy units", so standing behind your own minion wave body-blocks it. That is a concrete, repeatable way for Teemo to refuse his only non-ult poke, and it appears nowhere in the entry.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood costs him health and can be blocked by units — hold the wave between you and take none of it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (E Tides of Blood: "can be blocked by enemy units"; R Hemoplague)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text says Vladimir "out-ranges you with Hemoplague at 6+".
audit.why: Hemoplague is 625 range and Teemo's Q and autos are 680, so Teemo holds the longer reach — Vladimir has to step inside Teemo's range to land his ult. The entry has the range relationship backwards, which turns a positional edge for Teemo into a reason to back off.
audit.corrected: Hemoplague reaches 625 to your 680 — he steps into you, not the reverse.

audit.whatIsWrong: The pool is described only as "dodges your poke" without saying how.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool grants 2 seconds of untargetability. That is why a cast Blinding Dart fizzles on it rather than being merely mitigated, and it is why the counterplay is baiting the pool with a cheap auto rather than leading with Q.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool = 2s untargetable, so a targeted Blinding Dart fizzles. Bait it with an auto first.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (W flags untargetable, "becoming untargetable for 2 seconds")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] ("Lvl 4-5") says "zone him off his half of the wave with mushrooms at the tribush"; mid says "your shrooms seal tribush and the lane brushes" in its levels 4-5 passage. Both also say Q is "near-maxed".
audit.why: Noxious Trap is the ultimate, so there are no mushrooms before 6 — and Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank, so "near-maxed Q" buys duration rather than a faster loop.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 are spacing only; mushrooms at 6; blind is 7s flat.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Blinding Shot" in spikes[0].text, wants.you[0], wants.foe[1], whys[1]; "Liandry's Angueur" in spikes[2].text.
audit.why: Teemo's Q is Blinding Dart. "Liandry's Angueur" is not a real item; the full layer writes Liandry's Torment.

edits.before: At level 1 Vladimir's only tool is his Q Transfusion — it heals him and pokes, but it costs health, so auto-poke him back during the health-cost window before the heal resolves. The moment you hit level 2, every time he walks up to Q you hit Blinding Shot first: his autos miss, your E poison ticks, and his heal barely covers the exchange deficit. The critical rule these three levels is to never commit your Q while his Sanguine Pool is available — he simply pools through it, you waste the blind, and he wins the trade free. Bank small leads, keep the wave slightly toward your side, and let his weak level 1-3 health-cost pattern bleed him into a freeze you can exploit.
edits.after: At level 1 Vladimir's only tool is his Q Transfusion — it pokes and heals him and it costs him nothing at all, so there is no cost window to wait out; you simply have to win the auto exchange outright. The moment you hit level 2, every time he walks up to Q you hit Blinding Dart first: his autos miss, your E poison ticks, and his heal barely covers the exchange deficit. The critical rule these three levels is to never commit your Q while his Sanguine Pool is available — he simply pools through it, you waste the blind, and he wins the trade free. Bank small leads, keep the wave slightly toward your side, and remember the health cost in his kit is Tides of Blood, not Transfusion.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your cleanest control window: Q is near-maxed, your shrooms seal tribush and the lane brushes, and Vladimir has no good way to engage without his pool. The trade pattern here is rigid — poke with E auto, disengage with W, and the moment Sanguine Pool flashes on cooldown you re-engage for a full Q-blind auto chain while he takes the full DoT with no escape valve. At level 6 his Hemoplague ult changes the math: a well-timed R into your position deals massive burst and amplifies all your incoming damage by 10%, so never take an extended all-in at 6 without first confirming his R is spent. Use your own level 6 to plant shroom rings on every jungle path he might use to scale safely or roam — turn the map hostile and force him to farm under pressure.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your cleanest control window, though mushrooms do not arrive until 6: your blind is a flat 7s at every rank, and Vladimir has no good way to engage without his pool. notes: Two errors here were pointing the player at windows that do not exist: Transfusion was described as costing health (it is free — Tides of Blood is the health-cost ability), and Sanguine Pool's cooldown was given as 26s, which is not its value at any rank. Both were load-bearing for the trade rhythm. The Tides-of-Blood body-block is the best unused piece of counterplay in the matchup and I marked it Medium confidence because it rests on Riot's phrase "can be blocked by enemy units" rather than a Wiki check — worth confirming before it ships. Also note the packet's suspectNames were unusually accurate here (5 flags, 4 genuine); "Sanguine Pool's" was the only false positive. WKM_LINES not inspected.
